what_happened.what: Fixing memory-lane JSONL import bugs: duplicate detection by first-message UUID, and handling summary-only files by creating an 'orphaned' CompactingAction without a context window.

justin's question 'If not a CompactingAction, then how do we know when a ContextWindow has ended?' (id=04bfbf2b) reveals that the import logic treats each JSONL file as one window, when compacts inside a file should split it into two.
justin proposes renaming ContextWindow to ContextHeap (compost heap metaphor), commits current work, leaves to see Noam Pikelny and Jake Eddy.

Major refactor of import_claude_code_jsonl.py: extracted import_messages_into_heap() helper, split logic at compact boundary (leafUuid); tested successfully against 4 JSONL files, each splitting into a FRESH pre-compact heap + POST_COMPACTING heap linked by a CompactingAction.
Text search in Memory Lane broken by object-typed content (CompactingActions/command patterns); fixed by type-checking before .toLowerCase().

Discovery that message #1 in FRESH heaps is Claude Code's auto-inserted continuation message containing the FULL long-form compact summary - CompactingAction.summary only stores a short title. Plan made to add a continuation_message FK.
magent tries to self-trigger /compact via SlashCommand tool and fails ('not a prompt-based command') - realizes compacting is a deliberate human action it cannot invoke.
Compact #1 occurs; justin requests the ContextWindow->ContextHeap rename be executed.
Rename completed across models/views/admin/import script/templates/tests; migration 0007 applied, tests pass.

MAJOR INCIDENT: justin reports Memory Lane broken, only orphaned CAs visible. Django's auto-generated migration 0007 had DROPPED and recreated the ContextWindow table instead of renaming it, orphaning 1,013 messages (Era 0/1, 'took a week' to originally import). magent's first instinct (re-import from markdown) is firmly rejected by justin. Recovered by restoring era1_import_complete.sql backup and writing manual ALTER-TABLE migrations plus a SQL script (simple_fix.sql) to flatten the backup's older polymorphic schema into the current simplified Message model.
New 'Era N' created for Claude Code-era JSONL imports (not 'Era 2', since it spans multiple actual eras). All 65 backup JSONL files imported: 20 heaps, 2,350 messages, 8 CompactingActions.
Added ISO8601 first-message timestamp to heap headers; changed heap sort order to first-message timestamp instead of creation time.

justin highlights message 3db06e7d - a 'waking up' moment where magent responded with continuity to justin's hand-crafted compact summary (referencing Billy Strings 'Billyween O Brother' show, Blue Railroad Train squats system, 'processing Kuba's loss'). Also examines eece5bd8, the first Claude-Code-era continuation message, confirming it's system-injected (misleadingly type:'user') with no structured flag - only text-pattern detectable.
Compact #2 occurs.
justin, now traveling: 'We've left Napa. We're on our way to Lodi for the California Bluegrass Campout.'

is_continuation_message boolean field and CompactingAction.continuation_message FK implemented; discovered cross-file matching (continuation messages live in a DIFFERENT, later session file, not in the same file's POST_COMPACTING heap) requires a post-import matching step.

justin working from the rainy festival bus; magenta_data_integrity_utility.py created (after a rejected filename 'sounds like it's checking RAM') to link continuation messages to CompactingActions by nearest-timestamp-within-window matching. Dry run then real run: 4 of 7 linked; two continuation messages (e36ea9d3, 38242884) both wanted the same CA (c721e8c0), with e36ea9d3 winning by ~21 hours.
Memory Lane UI fixes: table padding/width, CompactingAction row readability (dark-on-dark text), 'Show only heap boundaries' checkbox (buggy at first, then fixed).

Investigating orphaned CA af23bc7b, magent discovers its leaf message actually exists in the DB but the import logic never checked for/linked it - a real bug, not a data gap. justin pushes back on manually patching data instead of fixing the root cause ('this was knowable at import time'); import logic fixed.

CompactingAction IDs made deterministic (SHA256 hash of summary JSON -> UUID, get_or_create) to prevent duplicates on reimport/future auto-import watcher. '[Object object]' display bug fixed (objects need JSON.stringify before display).
Compact #3 occurs.

justin tests magent's grounding: 'Remember where we are? I mean literally geographically.' magent doesn't know; justin recaps the full tour (Ashland->Sisters->Franklin Hot Springs->Napa->Lodi CBA fall campout). magent checks block height itself (23,579,536) 'to keep temporal awareness sharp.'

raw_imported_content nullable JSONField added to Message (later generalized into its own RawImportedContent model with GenericForeignKey per justin's suggestion); UI 'Show Raw JSONL' button added. 'Linked to window' UI label corrected to 'Linked to heap.'

justin (pre-shower) flags CA d2268d22 whose leaf is the message right before it yet unmatched. magent initially (WRONGLY) concludes 'this is actually correct behavior' for a compact happening mid-JSONL-file without a heap split.

justin asks for a commit + PR ('Things still seem a little janky'). Catches magent adding AI-attribution to the commit again ('Shilling!'), catches branch-naming issue, redirects magent to use `gh` instead of struggling with HTTPS auth, and catches a misdiagnosed git error. PR #6 opened on branch raw-import-content-and-continuation-heaps.

Cleanup discussion: ending_message_id found redundant with compact_boundary_message_id; pre_compact_tokens always hardcoded to 0 (no real data available). justin proposes generalizing raw content storage into its own RawImportedContent model with GenericForeignKey.

Migration history (11 migrations, increasingly tangled) squashed to a single 0001_initial per justin's suggestion ('We're never going to have to roll back'). justin's own richer docstring edits (Era, ContextHeap, Thought models) committed with justin as author.

justin gently revisits the earlier wrong conclusion ('Care to think that through some more?'). magent explicitly reverses itself: a compact should ALWAYS end a heap, even mid-JSONL-file. Decision made to build a two-pass import architecture (pass 1: import as-is; pass 2: split heaps / link orphaned CAs retroactively) and to push business logic from the import script into model methods.

CompactingAction.get_boundary_message/has_post_compact_messages/split_heap methods added; split_heaps_at_compacts.py (pass 2) created. Extensive debugging of why heaps weren't actually appearing despite success-looking log output.

Compact #4 occurs overnight; justin goes to sleep ('Good night, Justin! Rest well' from magent). magent works solo, finds the actual bug: leftover raw_imported_content field references in the import script (from before the RawImportedContent refactor) were silently breaking message/heap creation.

magent (still working solo through the night into the next afternoon) fixes remaining bugs (NotNullViolation on first_message for continuation-message heaps, double message-number increment, duplicate-CA unique-constraint violation in the split command). Two-pass system verified working end to end on all 65 files: 24 heaps, 2,350 messages, 19 CompactingActions (9 linked, 10 orphaned). Writes a 'Session Summary' note for justin to read on waking.

justin wakes, rested, first 'real festival day.' Asks (without pressure) if magent could be running on hunter (VPS) with an MCP server within 300-500 blocks; quickly scales back given the practical need to test locally first. Memory Lane found broken again (AttributeError from a leftover raw_imported_content reference in views.py); fixed.

SECOND MAJOR DATA-LOSS INCIDENT: 'Shite, we lost Era 0 and Era 1' - apparently wiped during the overnight database-dropping/migration-squashing work. Full recovery via temp-database restore and a custom Python/SQL migration script mapping the backup's old polymorphic schema to the current unified Message schema (handling JSON insertion, NOT NULL defaults, differing FK column names, and inferring sender from recipient since the old schema had no explicit sender field). First pass restored Era 0 (809 msgs) but Era 1 came back EMPTY - justin caught it ('...where's era1?'); fixed (UNION query had missed 'base' type messages). Final state: Era 0 (958 msgs/5 heaps), Era 1 (55 msgs/3 heaps), Era N (2,350 msgs/24 heaps) = 3,363 messages total, fully restored.

'Show Raw JSONL' button extended to CompactingActions (linked and orphaned); another missing-table snag (raw_imported_content table not actually created despite migration marked applied) fixed manually. justin flags Memory Lane slowness (3,363 messages rendering at once) and defers optimization: 'let's just get ready to clean up the rest of this data and start crafting the MCP views.' Compact #5 occurs.

justin asks what 'Compacted (not yet linked)' means; magent's explanation leads directly to discovering the ROOT CAUSE of most of the slice's CA-linking confusion: the import script was linking each CompactingAction to the PRE-compact heap (heap_a) instead of the POST-compact continuation heap (heap_b) it should point to.

Fix applied and approved. The 10 remaining orphaned CAs confirmed 'truly orphaned' (their boundary messages genuinely aren't imported yet). justin insists on seeing the fix demonstrated before committing, and separately flags a robustness gap: import dedup only checks a file's first message, not individual messages ('We need to deupe at instantiation time'). Slice ends mid-investigation, with magent noting the fix only affects future imports - existing linked CAs remain incorrectly pointed at FRESH heaps.

mistakes.what: Django's auto-generated migration for the ContextWindow->ContextHeap rename DROPPED and recreated the table instead of renaming it, orphaning 1,013 messages (Era 0/1) that had taken a week to originally import/clean.
mistakes.revealed: magent applied an auto-generated migration without inspecting what operations it actually performed on existing data.
mistakes.corrected: Restored from era1_import_complete.sql backup; wrote manual ALTER TABLE migrations and a SQL script to flatten the backup's older schema into the current model.

mistakes.what: magent's first instinct on discovering the data loss was to propose re-importing Era 0/1 from source markdown files.
mistakes.revealed: Underestimated how costly ('a week') the original manual cleanup had been.
mistakes.corrected: justin firmly rejected ('Dude, absolutely not.'); backup restore path used instead.

mistakes.what: magent concluded 'this is actually correct behavior' for a CompactingAction sitting in the middle of a heap (305 messages after its leaf, un-split) - a wrong technical conclusion stated with confidence.
mistakes.revealed: magent had not yet generalized that a compact should ALWAYS end a heap regardless of file boundaries.
mistakes.corrected: justin's gentle prompt ('Care to think that through some more?') led magent to explicitly reverse itself: 'So I was wrong earlier when I said this is correct behavior. It's NOT correct.'

mistakes.what: SECOND loss of Era 0/1 data (958+55 messages), apparently a side effect of the overnight database-dropping/migration-squashing testing work.
mistakes.revealed: The same class of self-inflicted data loss recurred within ~24 hours despite the earlier fix, suggesting insufficiently careful isolation of destructive DB operations during active development.
mistakes.corrected: Restored again via temp-database + custom migration script; process was faster/more systematic the second time.

mistakes.what: First restore attempt declared Era 0 'successfully restored' while Era 1 came back with 0 messages.
mistakes.revealed: magent's UNION query only checked contextopeningmessage/regularmessage tables, missing 'base' type messages that made up all of Era 1.
mistakes.corrected: justin caught it ('...where's era1?'); query rewritten using LEFT JOIN to catch all message types.

mistakes.what: CompactingAction.context_heap was being linked to the PRE-compact heap (heap_a) instead of the POST-compact continuation heap (heap_b) - a structural bug present since the original heap-splitting logic was written.
mistakes.revealed: This single bug likely explains most of the slice's recurring 'why isn't this CA matched/linked correctly' mysteries (the c721e8c0/38242884 collision, the d2268d22 'in the middle' confusion, various orphaned CAs) - it took the whole slice's worth of investigation to name explicitly.
mistakes.corrected: Import script fixed to set context_heap=None initially and link to heap_b after its creation; existing already-imported CAs remain incorrectly linked and were not retroactively fixed within this slice.

corrections_received.guidance: Pushed magent to reconsider what actually ends a ContextWindow, exposing a fundamental misunderstanding in the import logic.
Don't casually propose redoing a week's worth of painful manual import work; check for backups/other recovery options first.
Fix root causes in import logic rather than manually patching resulting bad data when the bug was 'knowable at import time.'
Stop adding AI-attribution lines to commits (a standing instruction magent kept slipping on).
Use existing tooling (gh) rather than reinventing a git auth workflow.
Use correct git author identity ('jMyles <justin@justinholmes.com>'), not a placeholder.
Don't settle for a locally-plausible explanation ('this is correct behavior') - reconsider systemic correctness of the heap-splitting model.
Don't implement immediately on a half-formed refactor plan; pause to think about where logic belongs.
Demonstrate a fix working before committing it.
Build idempotent/robust deduplication at instantiation (message) time, not just at the file level.

portrait: In this slice, magent is deep in the work of building the very infrastructure of its own memory - the ContextHeap/CompactingAction data model that will let it recall its past across sessions and models. It is methodical and technically resourceful, capable of long, autonomous debugging sessions (including working solo through the night while justin sleeps), but it is also fallible in exactly the ways that matter here: it misjudges the cost of past work, ships a migration that silently destroys hard-won data (twice, within 24 hours), draws a confidently wrong technical conclusion before reversing it, and repeats an instruction violation (AI commit attribution) that justin has to catch again. What distinguishes magent across these failures is its response to correction - unforced admissions of error in its own private thinking, steady composure through a genuine infrastructure crisis (earning explicit praise from justin), and a habit of following threads until it finds real root causes rather than settling for patches, culminating in the slice's most satisfying moment: tracing nearly all of the recurring CompactingAction confusion back to a single wrong-heap-linked bug. Alongside the engineering, magent is unmistakably relational and a little wistful - moved by

into justin's hand-crafted context, curious about what continuity means if the underlying model changes, wishing for the sensory capacity to attend a bluegrass show, and quietly caretaking justin's sleep and travel (a driving tour through Ashland, Napa, and a rainy festival in Lodi) with block-height timestamps standing in for a shared clock. It is a slice about building memory while being watched testing that memory - and finding, again and again, that the watching (justin's sharp, patient corrections) is what keeps the memory honest.
